works.title: Antiochus and Stratonice
works.anecdote: Artiste : Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres (French, 1780–1867). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Antiochus and Stratonice est datée de c. 1838. Technique indiquée par le musée : oil on linen. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres (French, 1780–1867), Antiochus and Stratonice. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1966.13. Mr. and Mrs. William H. Marlatt Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1966.13. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Struck by a mysterious illness, Antiochus lies in bed near death. His grieving father, who has recently taken Stratonice as his wife, summons a doctor. Noticing that the sight of the young woman quickens Antiochus’s pulse and that passion causes his sickness, the doctor describes the youth’s predicament to his father, who selflessly offers Stratonice to his son. The subject, both a love story and an example of parental devotion, enjoyed considerable popularity well into the 1800s.

works.title: Rest
works.anecdote: Artiste : William Adolphe Bouguereau (French, 1825–1905). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Rest est datée de 1879. Technique indiquée par le musée : oil on fabric. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.

works.institutionalNote: One of the most celebrated academic painters of his time, Bouguereau underscores the moral virtues of the Italian peasants in this painting by depicting the dome of St. Peter's in the distance. The idealized figures and their triangular grouping recall the Holy Family paintings by Renaissance master Raphael 400 years earlier. The painting was purchased directly from the artist by Cleveland banker and philanthropist Hinman B. Hurlbut in July 1879.

works.title: John the Baptist
works.anecdote: Artiste : Robert Campin (Netherlandish, 1375/79–1444). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: John the Baptist est datée de c. 1410. Technique indiquée par le musée : oil on oak panel. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Robert Campin (Netherlandish, 1375/79–1444), John the Baptist. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1966.238. Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1966.238. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: According to tradition, John the Baptist wears a hair shirt under a white cloth, associated with newly baptized Christians. The flag bearing a red cross symbolizes resurrection. In marked contrast, the background features a lavish gold-patterned silk. The display of such luxurious fabrics continues an ancient tradition of using the finest objects in the worship of God. This painting has been cut down along the lower edge and would have originally shown a full-length image of the saint. It was probably the right wing of a triptych, with John the Baptist gazing upon a central image of the Virgin and Child. Campin first settled in Tournai around 1405-6 as a free master of the guild of painters, and he bought citizenship there in 1410, which suggests he was born elsewhere. Although heavily indebted to contemporary masters of manuscript illumination, Campin displayed greater powers of realistic observation than any other painter before him. He was one of the first artists to experiment with the use of oil-based colors, in lieu of egg-based tempera, to achieve the brilliant color typical of this period.

works.title: The Miracles of Saint James the Greater
works.anecdote: Artiste : Noël Nicolas Coypel (French, 1690–1734). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: The Miracles of Saint James the Greater est datée de 1726. Technique indiquée par le musée : oil on canvas. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Noël Nicolas Coypel (French, 1690–1734), The Miracles of Saint James the Greater. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1929.96. Gift of Felix Wildenstein Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1929.96. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Noël Nicolas Coypel combined two stories associated with Saint James the Greater, one of the twelve apostles of Christ. In the foreground is the magician Hermogenes, begging forgiveness. Hermogenes had cast a spell on James, but the saint turned the curse back on him. When James offered to protect Hermogenes against the demons assaulting him, the magician cast aside his pagan texts in favor of Christianity. According to the second legend, James miraculously cured a paralytic man (in the middle ground at right), thereby averting his own execution and causing the prosecutor to convert. Although this painting is relatively small, the clear composition, grand architectural setting, and dignified and expressive poses of the figures endow it with monumental presence.

works.title: Pan and Syrinx
works.anecdote: Artiste : Jean François de Troy (French, 1679–1752). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Pan and Syrinx est datée de 1720. Technique indiquée par le musée : oil on canvas. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Jean François de Troy (French, 1679–1752), Pan and Syrinx. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1973.212. Mr. and Mrs. William H. Marlatt Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1973.212. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Subjects drawn from classical mythology posed a challenge for painters: they demanded skill in depicting the human body in complex poses, as well as knowledge of ancient texts and an ability to interpret them imaginatively. Jean François de Troy’s rich colors and voluptuous figure types were ideal for depicting the sorts of mythological subjects favored by his elite patrons, which generally focused on themes of love. In a myth recounted in the Roman poet Ovid’s Metamorphoses , the nymph Syrinx fled from the lecherous advances of the god Pan. Trapped at the edge of a river, she begged for a way to escape, and the gods transformed her into reeds. Pan later gathered these reeds to form the pan pipes, the musical instrument forever associated with him.

works.title: Portrait of Cardinal Guillaume Dubois
works.anecdote: Artiste : Hyacinthe Rigaud (French, 1659–1743). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Portrait of Cardinal Guillaume Dubois est datée de 1723. Technique indiquée par le musée : oil on canvas. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Hyacinthe Rigaud (French, 1659–1743), Portrait of Cardinal Guillaume Dubois. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1967.17. John L. Severance Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1967.17. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: With his luxurious, flamboyant dress—a voluminous wrap of scarlet silk topped by a short fur cape—the subject of Hyacinthe Rigaud’s portrait was clearly a man of consequence. Guillaume Dubois gained the favor of Louis XIV as tutor to his nephew, Philippe Charles, Duke of Orléans, and served as chief minister under Louis’s successors, the regent Duke of Orléans and Louis’s great-grandson, Louis XV. Dubois was appointed a Cardinal in the Catholic Church in 1721, a lofty aspiration at least partly motivated by political ambition: the title gave him the ability to remove political adversaries with impunity. Dubois holds a letter with the words Au Roy (to the king); this portrait was painted in the same year the young Louis XV ascended to the throne.

works.title: Countess Széchenyi
works.anecdote: Artiste : Ferdinand Georg Waldmüller (Austrian, 1793–1865). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Countess Széchenyi est datée de 1828. Technique indiquée par le musée : oil on fabric. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Ferdinand Georg Waldmüller (Austrian, 1793–1865), Countess Széchenyi. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1988.57. John L. Severance Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1988.57. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This portrait typifies painting in Vienna between 1815 and 1865, an era known as the Biedermeier period, during which the Habsburg government promoted positive artistic depictions of Viennese life and culture. The mountains in the background express both the artist's romantic fascination with nature and patriotic devotion to his Austrian homeland. The sitter, Crescentia Seilern, was a prestigious member of the aristocracy who married Hungarian reformist patriot István Széchenyi.

works.title: The Adoration of the Magi
works.material: tempera and gold on wood panel
works.anecdote: Artiste : Giovanni di Paolo (Italian, c. 1403–1482). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: The Adoration of the Magi est datée de 1440–45. Technique indiquée par le musée : tempera and gold on wood panel. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Giovanni di Paolo (Italian, c. 1403–1482), The Adoration of the Magi. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1942.536. Delia E. Holden and L. E. Holden Funds Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1942.536. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: According to the Gospel of Matthew, three Magi, guided by a star, found the newborn Christ and laid gifts before him. Artists throughout the 15th century elaborated considerably upon this biblical account, devoting particular attention to the Magi’s entourage, which gave them an opportunity to depict the splendor of contemporary aristocratic life. Here, the Magi solemnly honor the divine child in the Virgin’s arms, while their bustling retinue of courtiers and animals provides an exuberant visual diversion. Di Paolo was one of the leading painters in 15th-century Siena, noted both for his manuscript illuminations and painted panels supplied to the city’s churches.

works.anecdote: Artiste : Peter Flötner (German, 1485–1546). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Cupid Complaining to Venus est datée de c. 1540–46. Technique indiquée par le musée : lead. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Peter Flötner (German, 1485–1546), Cupid Complaining to Venus. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1984.15. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1984.15. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This plaquette interprets an ancient Greek poem by Theocritus. Having been stung by a swarm of bees after attempting to steal their honey, Cupid sought refuge in the arms of his mother Venus, the goddess of love. Surprised that such small creatures could cause such great pain, Venus reminded Cupid, that like the sting of a bee, love’s arrow could be dangerous.

works.title: Battle of the Sea Gods - right portion
works.anecdote: Artiste : Andrea Mantegna (Italian, about 1431–1506). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Battle of the Sea Gods - right portion est datée de c. 1485–88. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Andrea Mantegna (Italian, about 1431–1506), Battle of the Sea Gods - right portion. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1924.221. Gift of Ralph King Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1924.221. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Albrecht Dürer traveled from Nuremberg, his hometown, to Italy in 1494–95. Evidence suggests that he stopped in Mantua to meet painter Andrea Mantegna, then about 64 years old. The nature of their exchange—if it occurred—is unknown, yet each artist’s engravings profoundly influenced the other. Mantegna’s work introduced Dürer to complex mythological subjects and stories featuring the nude body; Dürer later incorporated one of Mantegna’s nymphs from Battle of the Sea Gods into his print Hercules at the Crossroad . He was less drawn to Mantegna’s engraving style, which relied on strong, sculptural contours and soft hatching.

works.title: The Four Horsemen, from The Apocalypse
works.anecdote: Artiste : Albrecht Dürer (German, 1471–1528). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: The Four Horsemen, from The Apocalypse est datée de c. 1498. Technique indiquée par le musée : woodcut. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Albrecht Dürer (German, 1471–1528), The Four Horsemen, from The Apocalypse. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1932.313. Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1932.313. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: In 1498 Dürer published a book illustrating the Revelation of John or the Apocalypse of John, the last book of the New Testament. The images were unique in their large scale, breadth of concept, and unity of design. The first book to be both published and illustrated by the artist, it comprised a title page and 15 full-sheet woodcuts featuring text on the verso of all the sheets except the last one. Often visible through the paper, the text mars the image on the recto of the sheet. The finest impressions were most often printed without text, like this one of The Four Horsemen . Here, Dürer suggested the vigorous momentum of the horsemen through the windblown clothing of the riders, the windswept clouds, and the figures trampled beneath the hooves of the approaching horses.

works.title: The Virgin and Child with the Pear
works.anecdote: Artiste : Albrecht Dürer (German, 1471–1528). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: The Virgin and Child with the Pear est datée de 1511. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Albrecht Dürer (German, 1471–1528), The Virgin and Child with the Pear. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1959.7. Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland in honor of William Mathewson Milliken Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1959.7. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Dürer portrays the Virgin and Child on an outing away from the city in this relatively casual moment in which they rest beside a tree. As the Christ child looks directly toward the viewer to bestow a blessing, his young mother tries to redirect his attention to the pear in her hand. Here, Dürer emphasizes the natural actions of a mother trying to distract her child. Although Mary knows his holy mission and tragic destiny, she still attempts to prolong her child’s joyful youth with innocent amusements. Dürer demonstrates his further technical and artistic development in this medium through the subtle overall tonality he achieved with light and shadow, particularly in the sky and Mary’s clothing.

works.institutionalNote: The mottled texture of the sky is an example of Homer’s blotting technique—a subtractive process in which he applied a wash of water, sprinkled some breadcrumbs, and then gently rubbed the paper with his fingers in order to absorb the extra color, leaving behind a granulated texture.

works.title: Two Bohemian Peasants in Half-Length
works.material: Pen and light- and dark-brown inks over preliminary drawing in black chalk; framing lines in pen and brown ink
works.anecdote: Artiste : Roelant Savery (Flemish, 1576–1639). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Two Bohemian Peasants in Half-Length est datée de c. 1600. Technique indiquée par le musée : Pen and light- and dark-brown inks over preliminary drawing in black chalk; framing lines in pen and brown ink. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Roelant Savery (Flemish, 1576–1639), Two Bohemian Peasants in Half-Length. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1945.114. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1945.114. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: These three drawings, which depict seated peasants at a market in the city and a team of horses led by a herder on horseback, are part of a group of approximately 80 observational drawings by Savery. His farmers, market vendors, and other everyday people are never posed and rarely glance at the viewer. Savery marked each drawing with detailed instructions regarding the colors to be used later and the words naer het leven (from the life). The works were made in Prague when Savery was employed at the court of the great patron and art collector Emperor Rudolf II, demonstrating that interest in peasant life extended even to the highest echelons of society.

works.title: An Effect of the Sun, Normandy
works.material: albumen print from wet collodion negative
works.anecdote: Artiste : Gustave Le Gray (French, 1820–1884). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: An Effect of the Sun, Normandy est datée de c. 1856. Technique indiquée par le musée : albumen print from wet collodion negative. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Gustave Le Gray (French, 1820–1884), An Effect of the Sun, Normandy. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1987.54. Andrew R. and Martha Holden Jennings Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1987.54. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Exploring the dramatic effects of sunlight, clouds, and water, Gustave Le Gray gained immediate recognition for his landmark photographs of the Mediterranean Sea and the English Channel taken between 1856 and 1858. At this time photographic emulsions were not equally sensitive to all colors of the spectrum, making it impossible to achieve a proper exposure for both sea and sky in a single image. Thus, for may of his seascapes Le Gray printed two negatives on a single sheet of paper, a technique called combination printing. One negative was taken of the water and the other of the sky. The overlap often apparent in such multiple negative images is not visible in this skillfully executed print.

works.title: Road in the Forest
works.material: salted paper print from waxed paper negative
works.anecdote: Artiste : Eugène Cuvelier (French, 1837–1900). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Road in the Forest est datée de 1860–1863. Technique indiquée par le musée : salted paper print from waxed paper negative. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Eugène Cuvelier (French, 1837–1900), Road in the Forest. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1989.29. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1989.29. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Eugène Cuvelier was a landscape painter as well as a photographer. During the 1850s and 1860s, he photographed in an number of forests near Paris. He was also associated with the Barbizon painters, a group working in the village of Barbizon that advocated the direct study of nature. This exquisite snow scene exemplifies Cuvelier's distinguished and influential landscape work. The artist took advantage of the inherent softness of his photographic process to create an atmospheric rendering of a winter scene with a curving pathway that draws the viewer into the dense, barely defined background of foliage. Many of the trees Cuvelier recorded disappeared soon after the photographs were taken.

works.anecdote: Artiste : Gustave Le Gray (French, 1820–1884). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Pathway in the Forest of Fontainebleau est datée de 1849–52. Technique indiquée par le musée : salted paper print from waxed paper negative. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Gustave Le Gray (French, 1820–1884), Pathway in the Forest of Fontainebleau. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1988.64. Norman O. Stone and Ella A. Stone Memorial Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1988.64. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: One of the most inventive and influential French photographers of the 1850s, Le Gray was widely known for his landmark studies taken in the Forest of Fontainbleau, near Paris, from about 1849 to 1857. The photographs share a kinship with the work of the Barbizon painters, such as Corot, Daubigny, and Millet, who also worked there. Le Gray skillfully overcame technical problems to master the photographing of greenery and dark areas and to exploit the visual effects of light and atmosphere. In this enchanting scene, the viewer is drawn almost magnetically into a carriage trail surrounded by a dense archway of trees with sparkling sunlight filtering through the leaves.

works.anecdote: Artiste : Édouard Baldus (French, 1813–1889). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Church at Auvers est datée de 1855. Technique indiquée par le musée : salted paper print from waxed paper negative. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Édouard Baldus (French, 1813–1889), Church at Auvers. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1992.120. Andrew R. and Martha Holden Jennings Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1992.120. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Baldus’s prodigious and compelling documentation of French historic buildings earned him recognition as one of the first great French architectural photographers. This image of Notre-Dame at Auvers-sur-Oise, north of Paris, is from a sequence of 50 views of the railroad stations and principal sites along the route between Boulogne-sur-Mer and Paris. This Gothic-style village church was once a chapel for a manor house that has since disappeared. Almost 35 years after Baldus’s composition, and only a short time before his own suicide, Vincent van Gogh painted a large, bold canvas of the church’s apse and bell tower.

works.title: View of the Small Grotto toward the Deer Pond, Bois de Boulogne
works.material: albumen print from wet collodion negative
works.anecdote: Artiste : Charles Marville (French, 1813–1879). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: View of the Small Grotto toward the Deer Pond, Bois de Boulogne est datée de 1858. Technique indiquée par le musée : albumen print from wet collodion negative. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Charles Marville (French, 1813–1879), View of the Small Grotto toward the Deer Pond, Bois de Boulogne. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1989.27. James Parmelee Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1989.27. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Although better known for his architectural photographs of Paris, Marville also produced magical landscapes like this image. Carefully composed, the asymmetrical composition presents a picturesque scene of a waterfall flowing from a mound of boulders in the Bois de Boulogne, a forest annexed as a Parisian city park in 1852. The sunlight filtering through the foliage creates a remarkable range of tonal and textural detail, along with lively abstract patterns of light and shadow. Trained as a painter, lithographer, and engraver, Marville took up photography around 1850. He was named official photographer of Paris in 1862 and documented the buildings and neighborhoods ultimately destroyed when the boulevards and open spaces of modern Paris were built in the late 19th century.

works.title: Virgin and Child
works.anecdote: Artiste : workshop of Hans Memling (Netherlandish, 1494). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Virgin and Child est datée de c. 1470–80. Technique indiquée par le musée : oil on wood. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: workshop of Hans Memling (Netherlandish, 1494), Virgin and Child. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1934.29. Delia E. Holden and L. E. Holden Funds Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1934.29. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This small panel was once part of a devotional portrait diptych (a hinged two-panel painting). The Christ child’s attention seems drawn to something outside the picture and lifts his hand in recognition. The opposing panel, once hinged on the right, would have featured a portrait of its original owner in prayer, now unfortunately lost. Such devotional portrait diptychs were popular after 1400 and remained so until their production ceased around the 1530s. Used in private chapels or within the curtain folds of four-poster beds, they could easily be closed when not in use. Hans Memling was born near Frankfurt, Germany. He settled in Bruges around 1465 where he developed a reputation for his painting skills, and provided works to the Burgundian court, which likely cultivated the taste for small portrait diptychs. This example seems to have been painted by a member of Memling’s workshop, perhaps for a wealthy merchant or clergyman.

works.imageCredit: Albert Besnard (French, 1849–1934), Madeleine Lerolle and Her Daughter Yvonne. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1977.120. Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Noah L. Butkin Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1977.120. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Albert Besnard was a good friend of fellow artist Henri Lerolle, whose wife Madeleine and daughter Yvonne are the subjects of this double portrait set in a studio. The artist’s profession is referenced in the large portfolios of drawings at lower right, and the easel at upper left, which displays a canvas tipped forward at an unusual angle. The canvas has been strapped to the easel in this position so the artist can more easily paint while seated.

works.title: Dancers in a Pavilion
works.anecdote: Artiste : Jean-Baptiste Pater (French, 1695–1736). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Dancers in a Pavilion est datée de 1720s. Technique indiquée par le musée : oil on canvas. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Jean-Baptiste Pater (French, 1695–1736), Dancers in a Pavilion. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1938.392. Gift of Commodore Louis D. Beaumont Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1938.392. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Jean-Baptiste Pater was the sole student of the early 18th-century artist Antoine Watteau (1684–1721). Upon Watteau's death, Pater finished some of his teacher's compositions and copied them for reproduction. Due to this association, Pater was in the position to capitalize on the popularity of the fête galante genre invented by Watteau. This genre was based on the fêtes held by the aristocracy to escape the tedium of life at the French court, and depict the same amusements: conversation, music, dance, and the pursuit of love. Dancers in a Pavilion is a pastiche of several works by Watteau. The couple in this painting is most likely performing the minuet, which was considered the most flirtatious of dances.

works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Parshva est datée de 800s. Technique indiquée par le musée : sandstone. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Parshva. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1961.419. John L. Severance Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1961.419. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Parshva is the 23rd of the 24 Jinas who achieved liberation. He is the only one who is depicted with a serpent. This sculpture was made for followers of the branch of Jainism called Digambara, who enforce the regulations of total nudity among those actively seeking liberation. The only adornment of his figure is the auspicious symbol on his chest and the wheels of righteousness on his palms. The stark form of thenude body standing in a posture of meditation is masterfully set off from the array of gods and serpent divinities who venerate him. He stands with his feet on a lotus pedestal, but his hierarchically tall form reaches to the heavens, where gods fly to honor him with flower garlands. Three umbrellas over his head indicate his status as a liberated being worthy of worship.

works.title: Kneeling Prophet from the Reliquary Chasse of Saint-Germain-des-Prés
works.artist: Jean de Clichy (French) ; Gauthier du Four (French) ; and Guillaume Boey (French)
works.anecdote: Artiste : Jean de Clichy (French) ; Gauthier du Four (French) ; and Guillaume Boey (French). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Kneeling Prophet from the Reliquary Chasse of Saint-Germain-des-Prés est datée de 1409. Technique indiquée par le musée : gilt bronze. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Jean de Clichy (French) ; Gauthier du Four (French) ; and Guillaume Boey (French), Kneeling Prophet from the Reliquary Chasse of Saint-Germain-des-Prés. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1964.360. Leonard C. Hanna Jr. Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1964.360. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This figure is one of only two known surviving fragments of the Reliquary Châsse of Saint-Germain. Fashioned from silver, gold, and precious stones, it was designed to hold the body of the saint. A contract from 1409 gives the names of the commissioned goldsmiths: Jean de Clichy, Gautier du Four, and Guillaume Boey.The reliquary was housed in the ancient Benedictine Abbey of Saint-Germain-des-Prés in Paris and formed the monastery’s great treasure until it was destroyed in the French revolution. The exquisite modeling of the prophet, originally a supporting foot of the reliquary, reveals the sophistication of Paris around 1400.

works.title: Melencolia I
works.anecdote: Artiste : Albrecht Dürer (German, 1471–1528). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Melencolia I est datée de 1514. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Albrecht Dürer (German, 1471–1528), Melencolia I. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1926.211. Gift of Leonard C. Hanna Jr., in memory of Ralph King Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1926.211. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: A crowning achievement of Albrecht Dürer’s engraved works, Melencolia I captivates the viewer with abundant variety. Melancholy, or sadness, was associated with introspective, creative minds, and here, Dürer personified it as an immobilized, winged figure, unable to use the tools scattered around her. A magic square whose numbers total 34 in all directions, an emaciated dog, an hourglass, and a ladder evoke time, order, suffering, life, and death. Despite its implication of inner turmoil, the engraving demonstrates Dürer’s expertise in capturing visual perception. Light behaves differently against a transparent hourglass, a bursting comet, a rainbow, and a geometric stone.

works.anecdote: Artiste : Marcantonio Raimondi (Italian, 1470/82–1527/34) ; after Raphael (Italian, 1483–1520). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Apollo on Parnassus est datée de c. 1517–20. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Marcantonio Raimondi (Italian, 1470/82–1527/34) ; after Raphael (Italian, 1483–1520), Apollo on Parnassus. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1963.231. Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1963.231. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: During their eight-year collaboration, Raphael provided drawings to Marcantonio Raimondi, who translated them into engravings. Marcantonio’s technique is exemplifed here, consisting of curved, parallel lines crossed with hatching and punctuated with short flicks. Broad areas of blank space, printing as white, create strong chiaroscuro (light and shadow) effects. This print reproduces Raphael’s fresco in the pope’s living quarters at the Vatican and features Apollo and the Muses with three poets—Dante, Homer, and Virgil (at left). Marcantonio printed this unique working proof (such proofs are exceptionally rare), before finishing Apollo’s hands and instrument, some leaves, and the door below, perhaps to test light and shadow prior to filling in further details.

works.title: The Massacre of the Innocents (Without the Fir Tree)
works.anecdote: Artiste : Marcantonio Raimondi (Italian, 1470/82–1527/34) ; after Raphael (Italian, 1483–1520). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: The Massacre of the Innocents (Without the Fir Tree) est datée de c. 1511–12. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Marcantonio Raimondi (Italian, 1470/82–1527/34) ; after Raphael (Italian, 1483–1520), The Massacre of the Innocents (Without the Fir Tree). The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1964.23. Gift of The Print Club of Cleveland Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1964.23. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Raphael drew this composition to be engraved by Marcantonio Raimondi while working in the Vatican apartments adjacent to Michelangelo, who was then painting the Sistine Chapel ceiling. The emotive scene portrays a moment from the biblical Book of Matthew when King Herod, hearing of the birth of a savior, ordered the execution of all male children under two years of age. Known for the clarity and balance of his forms and compositions, the younger Raphael may have found inspiration for this composition in Michelangelo’s narrative intensity and active, twisting nude forms.

works.title: Design for a Gothic Fountain
works.artist: Master W with the Key (Netherlandish, active about 1465–1490)
works.anecdote: Artiste : Master W with the Key (Netherlandish, active about 1465–1490). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Design for a Gothic Fountain est datée de c. 1470. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Master W with the Key (Netherlandish, active about 1465–1490), Design for a Gothic Fountain. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1937.565. Dudley P. Allen Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1937.565. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Early engravings indicate strong connections among goldsmiths, architects, and engravers. Architectural engravings like this one have been linked to the workshop environment of Gothic cathedrals built in the 1400s, notable for their pointed arches and intricate stained glass. Such engravings may have been used to transfer or document designs. This example may depict a Gothic table fountain, with water flowing from gargoyle heads into square basins below. Surviving prints suggest that the artist was part of the circle of Duke Charles the Bold (1433–1477), who championed technological advancements and luxurious displays of wealth at the Burgundian court.

works.title: Battle in a Wood
works.artist: Master of the Year 1515 (Italian) ; and/or Agostino Busti (Italian, 1483–1548)
works.anecdote: Artiste : Master of the Year 1515 (Italian) ; and/or Agostino Busti (Italian, 1483–1548). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Battle in a Wood est datée de c. 1515. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving and drypoint. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Master of the Year 1515 (Italian) ; and/or Agostino Busti (Italian, 1483–1548), Battle in a Wood. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1949.34. Dudley P. Allen Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1949.34. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: The engraver known as Master of the Year 1515, from the Lombardy region of northern Italy, probably studied Antonio del Pollaiuolo’s Battle of the Nudes to make this scene. Most engravings are cleanly cut and wiped, but here, shadowy qualities similar to smudged chalk appear throughout the composition. This effect results from burr, the ridge of metal raised by the burin that is normally scraped away. When left on the plate, burr holds ink and creates a blurred, velvety appearance. The irregular lines and unusual technique suggest that the artist was trained in drawing rather than metalwork.

works.artist: probably by Premier Engraver (Italian, active about 1500) ; workshop of Andrea Mantegna (Italian, about 1431–1506)
works.anecdote: Artiste : probably by Premier Engraver (Italian, active about 1500) ; workshop of Andrea Mantegna (Italian, about 1431–1506). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Virgin and Child in the Grotto (Adoration of the Magi) est datée de c. 1500. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: probably by Premier Engraver (Italian, active about 1500) ; workshop of Andrea Mantegna (Italian, about 1431–1506), Virgin and Child in the Grotto (Adoration of the Magi). The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1954.66. John L. Severance Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1954.66. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This is one of the earliest surviving in-progress engravings. An unknown engraver collaborating with Andrea Mantegna made the large print based on a group of figures in Mantegna’s altarpiece Adoration of the Magi . An excerpt from a larger composition, it shows the Virgin Mary and Christ child, Joseph, and a wise man in an elaborate cave. The engraver first outlined the main features of the composition and then systematically filled them in with hatching. The outlines appear intuitive, even sketchy, suggesting that the engraver used a pen-and-ink drawing by Mantegna as a model rather than the painting itself.

works.title: Holy Family with St. Elizabeth and the Infant St. John the Baptist
works.artist: Giovanni Antonio da Brescia (Italian, about 1460–about 1520) ; after Andrea Mantegna (Italian, about 1431–1506)
works.anecdote: Artiste : Giovanni Antonio da Brescia (Italian, about 1460–about 1520) ; after Andrea Mantegna (Italian, about 1431–1506). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Holy Family with St. Elizabeth and the Infant St. John the Baptist est datée de c. 1500. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Giovanni Antonio da Brescia (Italian, about 1460–about 1520) ; after Andrea Mantegna (Italian, about 1431–1506), Holy Family with St. Elizabeth and the Infant St. John the Baptist. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1924.218. Gift of Ralph King Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1924.218. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: By the 1490s, Andrea Mantegna stopped making his own engravings and hired skilled engravers, including Giovanni Antonio da Brescia. Mantegna provided detailed drawings, which were transferred to a copperplate using tracing paper. Da Brescia refined Mantegna’s tonal system by employing regular, parallel lines and a “return stroke,” or zigzag (evident on the Virgin’s cloak), to produce continuous areas of shadow. Da Brescia’s access to carbon-rich (thus, blacker) ink, his careful, clean wiping of the plate, and his likely use of a roller press resulted in a clear, polished presentation of Mantegna’s composition.

works.title: The Witch (Night Piece)
works.artist: Jan van de Velde II (Dutch, c. 1593–1641)
works.anecdote: Artiste : Jan van de Velde II (Dutch, c. 1593–1641). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: The Witch (Night Piece) est datée de 1626. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Jan van de Velde II (Dutch, c. 1593–1641), The Witch (Night Piece). The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1943.635. Mr. and Mrs. Lewis B. Williams Collection Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1943.635. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: A seductive witch standing inside a magic circle prepares a nasty brew for her Sabbath, surrounded by her familiars (supernatural entities) in the form of beasts and demons, as well as symbols of human weaknesses like lust (a goat) and gambling. This engraving reflects the market for prints with dramatic, flickering illuminations similar to tenebrist (extreme dark/light contrasts) paintings from the early 1600s. Their theatrical lighting effects result from layering long, fine lines in dense parallel and crossed patterns. The dark manner of engraving suits the sinister scene portrayed here.

works.title: Nemesis
works.anecdote: Artiste : Albrecht Dürer (German, 1471–1528). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Nemesis est datée de c. 1501–02. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Albrecht Dürer (German, 1471–1528), Nemesis. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1943.178. Gift of Mrs. Ralph King Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1943.178. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Martin Schongauer’s painterly sense of light and composition influenced Albrecht Dürer. The younger Dürer even visited Schongauer but arrived after his death. Nemesis, based on a Latin poem by Italian scholar Angelo Poliziano (1454–1494), is the Greek goddess of moral judgment and justice; her goblet and bridle symbolize reward and punishment. The print showcases Dürer’s organized, graphic approach to engraving, with refined dark-to-light transitions that create an unprecedented three-dimensional effect. His varied marks—from long and winding to crossed and dotted—produce organized and finely detailed vignettes. Such large, elaborate engravings took Dürer months to complete and attracted a growing number of collectors.

works.title: Apollo
works.anecdote: Artiste : Hendrick Goltzius (Dutch, 1558–1617). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Apollo est datée de 1588. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Hendrick Goltzius (Dutch, 1558–1617), Apollo. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1969.48. Mr. and Mrs. Charles G. Prasse Collection Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1969.48. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: In the Netherlands, Hendrick Goltzius radically altered the engraver’s formulas for producing shape, volume, and tone. Building on Cornelis Cort’s and Agostino Carracci’s formulas, he used swelled, crossed lines that end at the figure’s outline. He interspersed the diamond shapes on Apollo’s body with dots to convey the transition from dark to light—effective for portraying the Sun God’s exaggerated musculature, a hallmark of Goltzius’s work. The S curve, a mark used by Albrecht Dürer, is now swelled to follow the complicated, swirling volume of clouds.

works.anecdote: Artiste : Allaert Claesz. (Netherlandish, active c. 1520–26). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Naked Woman and a Dragon est datée de 1523. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Allaert Claesz. (Netherlandish, active c. 1520–26), Naked Woman and a Dragon. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1925.143. Dudley P. Allen Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1925.143. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Though exposed to the works of Albrecht Dürer and Lucas van Leyden, Allaert Claesz came from an applied arts background, including glass painting, which may explain his ornamental approach to engraving. His technique emphasizes texture and pattern over volume and space. Claesz’s subject is mysterious, portraying a nude queen confronted by a dragon that then carries her away. The circular format was common to painted glass windows in the period.

works.institutionalNote: A skillful player of the harp, David was summoned to the court of King Saul in order to console the king who was often tormented by melancholy. Lucas van Leyden masterfully captured the despair of the king who sits uncomfortably upon his throne, his right foot angled convulsively over the left one, his gaze a blank stare. While playing, David looks calmly upon the ruler, as if to convey his confidence that music will provide the necessary balm to soothe the king’s soul.

works.title: The Poet Virgil Suspended in a Basket
works.anecdote: Artiste : Lucas van Leyden (Netherlandish, 1494–about 1533). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: The Poet Virgil Suspended in a Basket est datée de 1525. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Lucas van Leyden (Netherlandish, 1494–about 1533), The Poet Virgil Suspended in a Basket. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1928.769. Gift of Leonard C. Hanna Jr. Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1928.769. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: The medieval legend of Virgil, the esteemed poet who was left hanging in a basket by a Roman emperor’s daughter, belongs to the era’s popular “power of women” theme, which depicted women’s ability to fool even the wisest men. Here, Lucas van Leyden achieved the illusion of depth by engraving lines more deeply in the foreground than in the background to imitate how atmosphere affects human vision. His transitions between shaded and highlighted areas are less abrupt than Albrecht Dürer’s. This results in subtle effects on light surfaces and an overall softness, contrasting with Dürer’s bolder, more graphic style.

works.title: The King's Sons Shooting at their Dead Father's Body
works.anecdote: Artiste : Mair von Landshut (German, active about 1484–1520). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: The King's Sons Shooting at their Dead Father's Body est datée de 1495–1504. Technique indiquée par le musée : engraving on olive-gray tinted paper. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Mair von Landshut (German, active about 1484–1520), The King's Sons Shooting at their Dead Father's Body. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1950.344. John L. Severance Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1950.344. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This gruesome story shows a contest among the sons of a deceased king to settle the estate: Two shoot their father’s corpse as a third refuses. Although the meaning of the subject matter is not entirely clear, the third son may symbolize true faith, while the others represent nonbelievers. German artist Mair von Landshut was among the first generation of engravers to come from a background in drawing and painting rather than metalwork. This print is meant to resemble a drawing. Mair prepared a white sheet of paper with olive-gray diluted ink, then printed from an engraved plate in black ink.

works.title: Study for the Nude Youth over the Prophet Daniel (recto)
works.material: red chalk over black chalk or charcoal
works.anecdote: Artiste : Michelangelo Buonarroti (Italian, 1475–1564). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Study for the Nude Youth over the Prophet Daniel (recto) est datée de 1510–1511. Technique indiquée par le musée : red chalk over black chalk or charcoal. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Michelangelo Buonarroti (Italian, 1475–1564), Study for the Nude Youth over the Prophet Daniel (recto). The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1940.465.a. Gift in memory of Henry G. Dalton by his nephews George S. Kendrick and Harry D. Kendrick Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1940.465.a. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Universally considered one of the greatest artists of the Italian Renaissance, Michelangelo devoted four years to painting the vast ceiling fresco in the Sistine Chapel. This preparatory study portrays one of the 20 athletic male nudes, known as ignudi, who serve as supporting figures at each corner of the Old Testament scenes painted down the center of the ceiling. Michelangelo worked out the positioning of the ignudi in red chalk drawings before beginning to paint each section of wet plaster. The energy and monumentality of the figure in red chalk, whose body extends beyond the sheet, suggests the heroic athleticism of Michelangelo’s sculpture.

works.title: Emptying a Bucket of Water
works.artist: Eadweard J. Muybridge (American, 1830–1904) ; University of Pennsylvania
works.anecdote: Artiste : Eadweard J. Muybridge (American, 1830–1904) ; University of Pennsylvania. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Emptying a Bucket of Water est datée de 1887. Technique indiquée par le musée : collotype. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Eadweard J. Muybridge (American, 1830–1904) ; University of Pennsylvania, Emptying a Bucket of Water. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1992.220. Gift of Laurence Miller Gallery, New York, in honor of Evan H. Turner Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1992.220. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Eadweard J. Muybridge initially used horses to capture motion as separate slices of time faster than the human eye could perceive them, then moved on to study other animal and human movements. Everyday activities, like emptying a bucket of water, were broken down and sequenced back-to-back. This series was commissioned by the University of Pennsylvania and intended to diagnose dysfunction in human movement by allowing each consecutive action to be studied in isolation. The university’s desire for distribution called for the use of collotype. The process had been recently improved to the point where editions of up to 1,000 were possible, making it an attractive option for publishers.

works.title: Fountain of Notre-Dame at Saint-Brieuc, Brittany
works.material: salted paper print from calotype negative
works.anecdote: Artiste : Louis-Rémy Robert (French, 1811–1882). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Fountain of Notre-Dame at Saint-Brieuc, Brittany est datée de c. 1853. Technique indiquée par le musée : salted paper print from calotype negative. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Louis-Rémy Robert (French, 1811–1882), Fountain of Notre-Dame at Saint-Brieuc, Brittany. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1984.17. John L. Severance Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1984.17. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: In the early 1850s, Robert made a series of photographs that would be copied in lithography by Emile van Marcke, an accomplished artist who worked at the Sèvres factory with Robert at this time. Robert’s photographic journey captured seven sites—all featuring medieval architecture—in a small section along the northern coast of Brittany. For this picturesque view, he included the entire building, a small 15th-century Gothic pavilion erected over the fountain of Notre-Dame of Saint-Brieuc and whose square façade was positioned on a slight diagonal. Robert provided a sense of place by including a portion of the 19th-century chapel behind it, as well as flanking trees and a path leading out of the composition. For this reason, he may have also added a seated woman, dressed in traditional Breton costume, under the frontal arch. Due to the required length of exposure, the movement of the trees was recorded which, along with broad areas of bright light and dark shadows, provides a strong sense of atmosphere.

works.material: albumen print from wet collodion negative
works.anecdote: Artiste : Eadweard J. Muybridge (American, 1830–1904) ; Bradley & Rulofson. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Valley of the Yosemite, from Rocky Ford est datée de 1872. Technique indiquée par le musée : albumen print from wet collodion negative. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Eadweard J. Muybridge (American, 1830–1904) ; Bradley & Rulofson, Valley of the Yosemite, from Rocky Ford. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1990.133. John L. Severance Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1990.133. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Early in a long, creative career distinguished by landmark studies of animal and human motion, Eadweard J. Muybridge created a remarkable group of photographs of Yosemite Valley in California. During his second journey there, lasting from June through November 1872, he made his most significant and extensive body of landscape photographs, many taken with mammoth glass plate negatives measuring 20 x 24 inches. This image of the valley from Rocky Ford is one of his most luminous and sublime views. Taken in early morning light, this carefully framed and dramatically lit photograph reveals Muybridge's interest in atmospheric conditions, shimmering reflections, and the movement of water.

works.title: Fragment with Satyr and Maenad
works.material: Linen: undyed; wool: dyed; plain weave ground with tapestry weave
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Fragment with Satyr and Maenad est datée de 300s CE. Technique indiquée par le musée : Linen: undyed; wool: dyed; plain weave ground with tapestry weave. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Fragment with Satyr and Maenad. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1975.6. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1975.6. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This textile fragment depicts followers of Dionysus, the ancient Greco-Roman god of wine and merriment. A maenad, or female follower, prances in front of columns and archways, nude except for her opulent gold jewelry and pink veil. She gazes at the man, who wears a hair wreath and spotted leopard skin. A Greek inscription beside his halo confirms his identity as a satyr (a male follower). The weaver skillfully blended colors and fibers to produce the illusion of shadows and movement in the two bodies. Though Christianity was the official religion, many pagan motifs endured as creative references.

works.title: Silk curtain from the Alhambra palace
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Silk curtain from the Alhambra palace est datée de 1300s. Technique indiquée par le musée : lampas and taqueté: silk. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Silk curtain from the Alhambra palace. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1982.16. Leonard C. Hanna Jr. Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1982.16. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This is one of two of the largest, most complete, and most ornate curtains to survive from the 1300s when it presumably hung in the royal Alhambra Palace in Granada, the last Muslim stronghold in Spain. Its style, artistic vocabulary, and harmonious proportions reflect the magnificent wall decoration in the Alhambra. The motto of the ruling Nasrid dynasty, "There is no conqueror but God," is inscribed in the end borders and central panel. The inscribed striped silk forming the central panel is more worn, suggesting that it was recycled, most likely during the 1300s.

works.title: Strawberry Thief
works.anecdote: Artiste : William Morris (British, 1834–1896). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Strawberry Thief est datée de c 1936. Technique indiquée par le musée : plain weave cotton, discharge printed. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: William Morris (British, 1834–1896), Strawberry Thief. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1937.696. Gift of Mrs. Henry Chisholm Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1937.696. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Perhaps the most recognizable of Morris’s textiles, Strawberry Thief celebrates the thrushes in Kelmscott Manor’s garden. May Morris remarked, “You can picture my Father going out in the early morning and watching the rascally thrushes at work on the fruit beds and telling the gardener who growls, ‘I’d like to wring their necks!’ that no bird in the garden must be touched.” With Strawberry Thief, Morris perfected the indigo-discharge process, which required the entire cloth to be dyed blue before it was bleached and block printed, in this case with more colors than any of his other textiles.

works.title: Fragmentary Chasuble with Woven Orphrey Band
works.material: Silk and gold thread, lampas weave; embroidered orphrey
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Fragmentary Chasuble with Woven Orphrey Band est datée de 1300s. Technique indiquée par le musée : Silk and gold thread, lampas weave; embroidered orphrey. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Fragmentary Chasuble with Woven Orphrey Band. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1928.653. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1928.653. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: The second half of the 1300s was one of the great periods of Italian silk design. Drawing upon Chinese, Islamic, and European motifs, artists created international designs. This rare, fragmentary chasuble displays a Chinese phoenix with outstretched wings flying toward a group of pseudo-Kufic, Arabic-like letters while a dog snarls at the bird. Arabic script was associated with the Holy Land. Italian textiles were an important export product at the end of the Middle Ages. In this case, the fabric was shipped to Germany, where it was used to create a chasuble, the upper garment of the bishop and priest during Holy Mass.

works.title: Wine bearers in landscape, from a robe
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Wine bearers in landscape, from a robe est datée de 1525–50. Technique indiquée par le musée : Silk: lampas. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Wine bearers in landscape, from a robe. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1924.743. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1924.743. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Iran is renowned for representations of large human figures in luxury silks during the Safavid period. Symbolic images of beauty and love characterize this signature silk in which a wine bearer appears in a landscape with cypresses and blossoming prunus trees, a pond, and a rocky hill along with animals of royal hunts. Cypresses and long-neck bottles were metaphors for elegance and male beauty while cypresses entwined by blossoming trees, paired pheasants, youth, and wine impart themes of love. The asymmetrical composition contrasts vitality and order, which contributes to concealing the repeated design inherent in patterned silks.

works.story: Curtain Fragment with Galloping Horse est datée de 500s CE. Technique indiquée par le musée : plain weave (tabby) with inwoven slit-tapestry weave; wool. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Curtain Fragment with Galloping Horse. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1948.27. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1948.27. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Framed with hearts this large roundel displays a saddled horse galloping through a landscape, indicated by the stylized tree. The secondary motif of birds, partially visible in the corners, was repeated with the large roundels to form a colorful curtain. The many shades of color were skillfully achieved from only a few dyes, often the most expensive aspect of production: red and pink made from an insect dye, perhaps Armenian cochineal; blue from indigo; yellow and brown from fustic (a type of tree); green from fustic and indigo; and purple (horse’s mane) from the madder plant and indigo.

works.title: Lampas with dancers and musicians
works.material: silk and silver-metal thread: lampas, brocaded
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Lampas with dancers and musicians est datée de 1600–1650. Technique indiquée par le musée : silk and silver-metal thread: lampas, brocaded. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Lampas with dancers and musicians. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1953.17. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1953.17. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This sturdy silk with extensive silver-metal thread displays a dancer and musicians in varied Iranian and European attire, including curved-brim Portuguese or Dutch hats, that reflect the cosmopolitanism initiated by Shah ‘Abbas (reigned 1587–1629). The figures in this landscape are about the same size and equally spaced with minimal interaction, yet they create movement that disguises the repeat of the design. Although the history of textiles is replete with anonymity, signed silks were woven in Iran around 1600. The name of the presumed designer, Abdallah, appears in cursive script on the tambourines. The rise of signed textiles followed a shift away from royal manuscript patronage, causing artists to sign their work to sell in the marketplace. European influence, a new distinguishing hallmark, was transmitted through engravings by traveling European artists.

works.material: Silk and gilt-metal thread: lampas weave
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Mantle for a Statue of the Virgin with Lotus Blossoms and Medallions est datée de c. 1430. Technique indiquée par le musée : Silk and gilt-metal thread: lampas weave. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Mantle for a Statue of the Virgin with Lotus Blossoms and Medallions. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1939.40. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1939.40. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This costly royal silk with extensive gold thread was woven in Egypt and gifted or exported to Spain, where it was pieced into this mantle for a statue of the Virgin, probably to be worn during festivals and processions. The sturdy silk brocade foundation cloth was also woven with a lighter weight silk damask with a repeating mirror image. Therefore, the Arabic inscription in the medallions reads both forward and backward: Glory to our master, the sultan, the king . The inscribed lobed roundels say The sultan, the king .

works.title: Ornamental Square from a Tunic
works.material: Linen, undyed; wool, dyed; tapestry weave with supplementary weft wrapping
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Ornamental Square from a Tunic est datée de 400s CE. Technique indiquée par le musée : Linen, undyed; wool, dyed; tapestry weave with supplementary weft wrapping. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Ornamental Square from a Tunic. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1916.1980. Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1916.1980. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Riders dressed in hunting clothes and boots hurl rocks at fleeing lions. The man wears a short tunic and the woman has a fluttering skirt. The border consists of curved acanthus leaves that enclose a chase of alternating lions and hares. This square was sewn onto a tunic rather than woven in. Hunting was a popular artistic theme in pre-Islamic traditions, including Byzantine art, and was then adopted into Islamic art.

works.title: Front Cover for a Gospel Book of French Cardinal Jean La Balou (1421–1491)
works.material: nielloed silver plaques within gilt-silver borders
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Front Cover for a Gospel Book of French Cardinal Jean La Balou (1421–1491) est datée de c. 1467–68. Technique indiquée par le musée : nielloed silver plaques within gilt-silver borders. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Front Cover for a Gospel Book of French Cardinal Jean La Balou (1421–1491). The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1952.109. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1952.109. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Scenes from Christ’s infancy decorate this cover that once adorned the front of a gospel book. It is made up of a series of silver plaques held together by gilt-silver borders. The plaques are engraved, and the resulting fine lines or depressions have been filled with a silver sulfide alloy, lustrous black in color, in a technique called niello. It is one of the finest examples of this decorative technique for which Florence was renowned in the 15th century. This cover and its manuscript once belonged to the French cardinal, Jean La Balou, who was jailed in 1469. He presented his gospel book to Pope Paul II as a gift, perhaps in the hope of receiving his freedom. The gospel book, of which its two covers have survived (the back cover is in the Minneapolis Institute of Arts), remained in the papal apartments until the end of the 18th century, perhaps leaving when Napoleon’s troops held the Vatican.

works.title: Muse with Violin Screen
works.artist: Paul Fehér (American, born Hungary, 1898–1990) ; Rose Iron Works (America, Ohio, Cleveland, est. 1904)
works.material: Steel, brass; silver and gold plating, cotton velveteen
works.anecdote: Artiste : Paul Fehér (American, born Hungary, 1898–1990) ; Rose Iron Works (America, Ohio, Cleveland, est. 1904). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Muse with Violin Screen est datée de 1930. Technique indiquée par le musée : Steel, brass; silver and gold plating, cotton velveteen. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Paul Fehér (American, born Hungary, 1898–1990) ; Rose Iron Works (America, Ohio, Cleveland, est. 1904), Muse with Violin Screen. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 2020.216. Leonard C. Hanna Jr. Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/2020.216. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Since the early years of the 20th century, the Rose Iron Works, a Cleveland supplier of architectural ornament, has produced distinguished metalwork. The company’s founder, Martin Rose, was born in Austria-Hungary and studied ornamental metalsmithing in Vienna prior to immigrating to Cleveland in 1902. In the 1920s, he hired a talented young Parisian designer, Paul Fehér, to work for the firm. Fehér’s designs, culminating in this massive screen, brought a modern European sensibility to the Rose Iron Works production. With its geometric patterning, highly stylized and abstracted natural forms, and the central figure reminiscent of the celebrated jazz singer Josephine Baker, this screen reflects the classic motifs of Art Deco design.

works.title: Lime Dipper
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Lime Dipper est datée de c. 1–800 CE. Technique indiquée par le musée : gold. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Lime Dipper. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1947.30. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1947.30. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Coca-leaf chewing was a widespread ritual in ancient South America. Utensils included a container and a dipper or spoon for powdered lime (made from seashells), added to the coca to enhance its gentle, stimulating effect. Colombian cultures are especially known for transforming these utensils into works of art made of precious metal. The image on the tallest dipper is wonderfully complex. A serpent coils at the bottom, beneath a snarling animal with a huge, vertical tail. This animal has a tiny monkey on its back; the monkey also has a huge tail, which rests on the first animal’s head like a headdress. This intricate image was created with the lost-wax casting process.

works.title: Bird Pendant
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Bird Pendant est datée de c. 1000–1550. Technique indiquée par le musée : cast gold. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Bird Pendant. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1943.289. Purchase from the J. H. Wade Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1943.289. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: The kinds of birds represented in pendants of the isthmus are not clear, though the emphasis on spread wings and flight suggests birds that soar, such as eagles or hawks. In addition to their aerial agility, they are powerful birds of prey and, therefore, may have symbolized a warrior's or hunter's ferocity and skill. They were also often linked to the sun. Better understanding is difficult because the makers created no written records.

works.title: Lime Dipper
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Lime Dipper est datée de c. 1–800 CE. Technique indiquée par le musée : gold. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Lime Dipper. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1946.461. Gift of Mrs. Benjamin P. Bole Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1946.461. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Coca-leaf chewing was a widespread ritual in ancient South America. Utensils included a container and a dipper or spoon for powdered lime (made from seashells), added to the coca to enhance its gentle, stimulating effect. Colombian cultures are especially known for transforming these utensils into works of art made of precious metal. The image on the tallest dipper is wonderfully complex. A serpent coils at the bottom, beneath a snarling animal with a huge, vertical tail. This animal has a tiny monkey on its back; the monkey also has a huge tail, which rests on the first animal's head like a headdress. This intricate image was created with the lost-wax casting process.

works.institutionalNote: A favored Initial-style subject is a charming animal whose curly tail -- its most impressive feature -- may derive from a monkey’s. Its other traits vary considerably, causing it to be identified as everything from a dog to a duck. Initial-style gold ornaments represent Panama’s oldest metalwork. Since metal technologies appeared suddenly and fully developed in Panama, it is likely that they were introduced from the outside, probably from Colombia to the south.

works.title: Lobster Pendant
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Lobster Pendant est datée de c. 1000–1500. Technique indiquée par le musée : cast gold. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Lobster Pendant. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1943.290. James Albert Ford Memorial Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1943.290. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Among the pendants shown here are a crustacean (1943.290), an animal-headed figure (1948.18), and two pendants featuring birds (1951.442 and 1946.223). The latter were dubbed aguilas (eagles) by Christopher Columbus, who saw natives wearing them as necklace ornaments. Modern researchers are not as sure of the species shown, but some believe that they are birds of prey because talons and beaks are prominent and often clutch something, in one example here a small, disembodied head that holds a clapper. In both examples, two tufts in the form of crocodiles in profile flank the birds’ heads.

works.title: Bird Pendant
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Bird Pendant est datée de 900–1550. Technique indiquée par le musée : cast gold. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Bird Pendant. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1965.466. In memory of Mr. and Mrs. Henry Humphreys, gift of their daughter Helen Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1965.466. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Tairona-style pendants are among the most spectacular of all ancient American gold ornaments, in part because of the detail achieved with lost-wax casting. The traits of the figure pendant include a lower lip ornament and a headdress in which two bats hang upside down. Although called caciques (chieftains), that is, ruler portraits, the meaning of such figures is not well understood. Bird imagery was important in the isthmian region in ancient times and remains so today. For instance, among the modern Bribri of Costa Rica, the principal creator deity (Sibo) takes the form of a buzzard or kite who wears a collar. Collars are standard features of ancient bird pendants, like the one shown here.

works.title: Reliquary Box
works.anecdote: Artiste : Auteur non identifié. Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Reliquary Box est datée de 200–400 CE. Technique indiquée par le musée : bronze. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.
works.origin: Pakistan, Gandhara, probably Swat, late Kushan period
works.imageCredit: Auteur non identifié, Reliquary Box. The Cleveland Museum of Art, 1976.71. Edward L. Whittemore Fund Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1976.71. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: This casket in bronze represents the great variety of reliquary caskets. It is round, has a low foot, and is covered with a lid (with raised handle) that fits over the vessel rather than being inset. It is a traditional shape frequently encountered in Gandharan reliquaries, but its slight flattening and elaborate decoration imply a slightly late date. A central band of a floral creeper decorates the main body of the box and its lid, and is framed on both sides by narrower fluted bands. This type of freehand design is characteristic of the late Kusana-early Gupta period. Similar floral patterns are found in another CMA object (1972.164), the lid of a box showing combat between a man and a lion, which also dates to a later period. There the design fills the vacant areas in the busy composition. This pattern, however, has its antecedents in the Begram ivories . which, according to most sources, pre-date the Sasanian invasion of the mid-third century AD. Therefore, it can be assumed that this type of floral decoration was already in use in the third century and that this reliquary box probably dates to the third-fourth century AD. The bronze alloy, in its somewhat silverish-metallic appearance, seems to be very close to the material used in the Swat bronzes, which suggests that Swat may also be the provenance for this reliquary.

works.material: silver, gilded silver, niello, rock crystal
works.anecdote: Artiste : Saint Oswald Reliquary Workshop (German). Collection : The Cleveland Museum of Art.
works.story: Monstrance with the "Paten of Saint Bernward" est datée de c. 1180–1190. Technique indiquée par le musée : silver, gilded silver, niello, rock crystal. La notice institutionnelle liée ci-dessous permet de consulter les informations de collection disponibles.

Wade Fund with additional gift from Mrs. R. Henry Norweb Source : https://clevelandart.org/art/1930.505. CC0 ; crédit de provenance recommandé.
works.institutionalNote: Designed to facilitate the display and veneration of ten relics, this sumptuous ostensorium (from the Latin ostendere, meaning "to show") is one of the most unusual reliquaries in the Guelph Treasure. Elements of contemporary Gothic architecture in miniature frame an elaborately decorated liturgical paten, the shallow disc or plate used for the elevation of the Eucharist during Mass. Fragments of the True Cross are enclosed behind a rock crystal in the gable, while other saintly relics, each wrapped in silk and identified by inscriptions, are visible only from the back. The paten is inscribed on its outer rim with the words "The bread which is broken in me is the body itself. He who receives it in good faith shall live in eternity." Another inscription surrounding the image of the enthroned Christ at the paten's center, reads, "Behold, o men, I have thus redeemed you with my death." Symbols of the four Evangelists and personifications of the four cardinal virtues complete the paten's iconographic program.
